recentItems.title: Are family doctors an endangered species? | Dr. Marie Elizabeth Ramas | TEDxPortsmouth
recentItems.description:
What happens when the one doctor trained to know your whole story — your history, your family, your fears — disappears? Dr. Marie-Elizabeth Ramas warns that family medicine is facing a crisis that will touch every one of us, and most people won't realize what they've lost until the moment they need it most.

Dr. Marie-Elizabeth Ramas is a family physician with 15 years of experience caring for patients across the full spectrum of life — from birth through end of life, in clinics, hospitals, and homes. As a doctor for largely non-English speaking and underserved communities, she has spent her career at the intersection of public health, advocacy, and whole-person care. A lifelong New Hampshire native, Dr. Ramas has been a voice for health equity and primary care access at the local, state, and national level. She practices what she preaches: she has a family doctor, and she thinks you should too. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Is your thinking garbage?  | Arthur Zards | TEDxArlington Heights
recentItems.description:
Arthur Zards, a meaning strategist, argues that progress is making more of our thinking automatic. And as answers become easier to get, choosing can start to replace thinking. Zards challenges us to build a simple thinking system that keeps our thoughts distinctly our own. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at: https://www.ted.com/tedx

Production By: Peaceful Luck Media
Graphics By: Lauren Schultz
 Arthur Zards has spent three decades working where technology, story, and human behavior meet.

In 1992, he co-founded one of Chicago’s first internet service providers, before the web browser existed. He was not studying the internet. He was building it. He became fascinated by a question that has followed him ever since: what happens when a new tool changes not just what we can do, but what we value?

He founded TEDxNaperville and spent fifteen years helping hundreds of speakers uncover the idea beneath what they knew and shape it into a story worth someone’s time. He has spoken at TEDActive and led workshops at numerous TED events. He built a practice in experience design, creating rooms, moments, and conversations that mean something.

Today those threads converge in Lab Z, where his keynotes, workshops, and advisory work help leaders and organizations protect their thinking and create meaning as AI makes answers nearly free.

He also built his own 850-pound wood-fired grill. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Can art help you find yourself again? | Phil Jackson | TEDxArlington Heights
recentItems.description:
Phil Jackson, an arts & justice innovator, reveals that art isn't just for kids; it restores and reconstructs identity. Jackson’s heartfelt stories invite you to consider how, when art becomes your weapon of choice, it creates space to reimagine your future within a new identity. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at: https://www.ted.com/tedx.

Production By: Peaceful Luck Media
Graphics By: Lauren Schultz 
 Phil Jackson, founder and pastor, has spent nearly four decades at the intersection of culture and community transformation, building innovative organizations that bridge faith, the arts, and community leadership.

He founded The House Covenant Church, widely known as The House - a groundbreaking hip-hop worship community that earned national recognition and has been featured on BET, MSNBC, PBS, The New York Times, and The Chicago Sun-Times.

He founded The Firehouse Community Arts Center of Chicago, a nationally recognized nonprofit housed in a restored 100-year-old firehouse.

Phil is the co-author of “The Hip-Hop Church” (InterVarsity Press), now in its 12th printing. He is a Midwest Emmy Award winner for “Chicago at the Crossroad” and hosts SiriusXM’s Holy Culture Radio program “Church on the Block.”

Phil holds a Master of Divinity from Northern Theological Seminary, and is a recipient of the Leaders of a New Chicago Award from the MacArthur Foundation and Field Foundation. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Why the best stories are polarizing | Maryam Mehrtash | TEDxArlington Heights
recentItems.description:
Maryam Mehrtash, a narrative strategist, makes the case that every story worth telling exposes tension, and that the stories we can’t stop watching are the ones we avoid telling in our own lives. Through the story of her grandmother, an Iranian Kurdish actress imprisoned for being a storyteller, she offers a simple way to turn toward the polarizing moment and stay in the conversation. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at: https://www.ted.com/tedx.

Production By: Peaceful Luck Media
Graphics By: Lauren Schultz
 Maryam Mehrtash spent nearly two decades inside Hollywood's biggest rooms, building campaigns for Paramount+, CBS, Disney, Marvel Studios, and 20th Century Studios. Her work spanned franchises like Star Trek, Yellowstone, and the GRAMMYs, and global brands from Google and Amazon to VISA and General Motors. A TV Week 40 Under 40 honoree and WIF Business Fellow, she spent years building narratives that made millions of people care.

Now she's building her own. Her Substack, This Is Not A Memo, hit the Rising Bestsellers list within 24 hours, and her first book is underway. She believes it's never too late to rewrite your story.

The daughter of Iranian immigrants who fled the revolution, Maryam is a heart attack survivor, a poet, and a board member of Waterwell and the Prohuman Foundation. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Can Your City Compete Without You?  | Bob Hess | TEDxArlington Heights
recentItems.description:
Bob Hess, a global location strategist, digs deep into what impacts the odds of your city winning attractive investments. Hess’s heartfelt stories reveal an unexpected factor that can help shape your city’s growth - and what’s at stake when it’s overlooked. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at: https://www.ted.com/tedx.

Production By: Peaceful Luck Media
Graphics By: Lauren Schultz
 Robert Hess is Vice Chairman of Newmark’s Global Occupier Solutions platform and a globally recognized leader in corporate location strategy, site selection, and business strategy. Over a 40-year career, he has led more than 350 projects, advising organizations on complex location and growth decisions. With more than 2.75 million air miles across the globe. 

Robert has held leadership roles as co-founder and Consulting Partner with Cushman & Wakefield’s Global Supply Chain Business Consulting Group and with Deloitte’s renowned Fantus Location Strategies practice. His expertise has been featured in The Wall Street Journal and numerous leading business and trade publications. 

His executive education includes MIT, Oxford, Harvard, Northwestern, Wharton, and IMD Switzerland. He is a founding member and shareholder of the Site Selectors Guild and recently served a two-year appointment on the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Investment Advisory Council Workforce Development Committee. recentItems.title: How to manage our fisheries with science and lived experience | Liberty Denman | TEDxCapeMay
recentItems.description:
When we talk about nature it’s often referred to as a separate entity, as if we ourselves are not part of the system. Given that we are, how can we blend lived-experience of those closest to this system and new technologies, to ensure we can balance the system for fish and fisher alike? Liberty Denman is a marine biologist, science communicator, and Co-Founder of Kai. Her work focuses on the relationship between people and marine ecosystems, with a particular interest in how knowledge moves between coastal communities, scientists, and decision-makers in the fisheries space. 

Drawing on experience across commercial and recreational fisheries, conservation and research, education and Ocean literacy, diving and marine technology, she examines how different groups understand and respond to change in the Ocean. Her current work explores how the expertise of fishers can be integrated into fisheries management and conservation using purpose-built technology. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Voice Unheard: Refending Equality | Salma Ranggita | TEDxTrisakti School of Management
recentItems.description: This talk sheds light on the voices that too often go unheard. Every day, many people live with unfair treatment, limited opportunities, and stories that are never given the space to be told. Equality is not only about laws and policies. It is also about listening, understanding, and making sure that no one is left behind simply because of who they are or where they come from. In this talk, Salma Ranggita shares why speaking up matters and how each of us has a role in defending equality, both in big movements and in small everyday actions. Through personal reflections and real experiences, the talk explores how silence can keep injustice alive, while courage and empathy can slowly break down the barriers that divide us. Sometimes, defending equality starts with something as simple as choosing to listen, asking the right questions, or standing beside someone who needs support. Change does not always come from the loudest voices, but from the people who refuse to stay quiet when it matters most. This talk encourages the audience to recognize the power of their own voice, to use it for those who cannot be heard, and to help build a world where everyone is seen, valued, and treated as equal. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx Salma Ranggita Cahyariyani is an Indonesian social activist, model and beauty pageant titleholder who was crowned Puteri Indonesia Pariwisata 2025, and she placed in the Top 21 at Miss Cosmo 2025. She is a University of Indonesia graduate in Metallurgical and Materials Engineering and Network Coordinator for SDSN Youth Indonesia. Her advocacy focuses on women in STEM, sustainability, and youth empowerment. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Değişirken Kendin Kalabilmek | Özlem ÖZKULAK | TEDxAtapark
recentItems.description: Hayat bazen bizi yeniden başlamaya, alıştığımız sınırların dışına çıkmaya ve kendimizi yeniden inşa etmeye zorlar. Peki, bütün bu değişimlerin içinde kendimiz olarak kalabilmek mümkün mü? 1973 yılında Uşak'ta dünyaya gelmiştir. Bir çocuk annesi olan Özkulak, reklamcılık ve proje danışmanlığı alanlarında çalışmıştır. Meslek hayatında ulusal bir gazetede reklam müdürlüğü yapmış, daha sonra kendi reklam ajansını kurmuştur. Uzun yıllar obeziteyle mücadele eden Özkulak, 110 kilodan 55 kiloya düşerek kendi hayatında önemli bir değişim yaşamıştır. Bu süreçte yaşadığı zorluklardan ve deneyimlerinden yola çıkarak 2018 yılında İzmir'de Obezite ve Sağlıklı Yaşam Fuarı düzenlemiştir. Daha sonra sağlık turizmine yönelerek Türkiye Sağlık Turizmi Derneği İzmir Temsilciliği görevini üstlenmiştir. Ayrıca Türk doktorlarını uluslararası alanda tanıtmak amacıyla Find Doctor in Turkey adlı platformu kurmuştur. Özkulak, kişisel deneyimini toplumsal farkındalık çalışmalarına dönüştürmesiyle öne çıkan isimlerden biridir. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: L’incontro come forza di cambiamento | Alberto Cecchini | TEDxBellagio
recentItems.description:
Alberto Cecchini è ingegnere e manager, con un lungo percorso internazionale tra infrastrutture, cooperazione e impegno sociale. Nel Rotary ha ricoperto incarichi di responsabilità a livello nazionale e internazionale, fino a far parte del Board of Directors del Rotary International, affiancando negli anni missioni umanitarie, progetti per l’eradicazione della poliomielite e iniziative dedicate alla pace, è inoltre tra i promotori di Time for Change, progetto che unisce arte, cultura e responsabilità sociale.
Il suo intervento nasce dagli incontri vissuti in Paesi e contesti molto diversi e da una domanda: cosa può realmente cambiare il nostro modo di guardare gli altri e il mondo che ci circonda?
Attraverso persone, luoghi e memorie che hanno segnato il suo percorso, emerge il valore dell’ascolto, dell’attenzione e dell’accoglienza, insieme alla capacità degli incontri di trasformare il nostro punto di vista.
Un viaggio che conduce a interrogarsi su dove cominci davvero la pace e sul ruolo che ciascuno di noi può avere nel costruirla.  A civil engineer, executive, and Sole Director and Technical Director of Idroesse Engineering, Alberto Cecchini built his professional career in major infrastructure, coordinating complex projects and operating within international contexts over the years. Since 2015, he has led the renewal and consolidation of Idroesse Engineering, a company carrying forward the legacy of Italian engineering excellence active since 1927.

Parallel to his career, for over thirty years he has maintained a strong commitment to international service and cooperation through Rotary. This journey led him to hold numerous leadership positions, culminating in his role as Board Director of Rotary International for the 2022–2024 term, engaging with diverse communities and global organizations worldwide This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Purpose Beyond Profit: Building What Matters | Bryant Kandani | TEDxTrisakti School of Management
recentItems.description: This talk challenges the idea that success is measured only by how much money we make. Profit keeps a business alive, but purpose is what gives it meaning. Behind every lasting brand, every loyal customer, and every team that truly believes in what they do, there is a reason that goes deeper than numbers on a financial report. In a world where businesses are judged not only by what they sell but also by the impact they leave, building something that matters has become more important than ever. In this talk, Bryant Kandani shares how purpose can become the foundation for decisions, growth, and long-term success. Through personal experiences and reflections, the talk shows how values, people, and positive impact can work hand in hand with profit instead of standing against it. Every product, every service, and every business decision is a chance to create value that reaches beyond the company itself and makes a real difference in people’s lives. This talk encourages the audience, whether aspiring entrepreneurs, professionals, or students, to rethink what success truly means and to start building things that matter, not just things that sell. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx Bryant Kandani is the founder of Frazier Agency, a personal branding agency that helps people grow their social media followers and engagement. He was a speaker at TEDxYouth@SmakOne 2024, where he explored the double-edged nature of social media. He is also reported to be the youngest Ironman finisher in Indonesia. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Başkalarının Sesiyle Kendi Hikâyemi Yazdım | Mehmet DİNDAR | TEDxAtapark
recentItems.description:
Birbirinden farklı seslere hayat verirken aslında kendi hikâyesini yazan Mehmet Dindar, taklit yeteneğinin ardındaki yaşam mücadelesini, hayallerini ve kendini keşfetme yolculuğunu anlatıyor. recentItems.title: Fireside Chat | Daniel Tani | TEDxBelgrade
recentItems.description:
Daniel Tani had the opportunity to see the world from a completely different perspective. What can his experience teach us about our planet and life on Earth? Having spent 132 days in space and completed six spacewalks, Daniel is sharing his experiences at TEDxBelgrade 2026, in a fireside chat with Nemanja Djordjevic, Managing Director of the Miodrag Kostic Endowment – Palace of Science in Belgrade.
|||||
Danijel Tani je imao priliku da vidi svet iz potpuno drugačije perspektive. Šta nas njegovo iskustvo može naučiti o našoj planeti i životu na Zemlji? Astronaut koji je proveo 132 dana u svemiru i izveo šest svemirskih šetnji, podelio je svoja iskustva na TEDxBelgrade 2026, u konverzaciji sa Nemanjom Đorđevićem, upraviteljem Zadužbine Miodraga Kostića - Palate nauke u Beogradu.
 Daniel Tani spent 132 days in space and completed six spacewalks during his 16-year NASA career. He first flew aboard Endeavour on mission STS-108 in 2001, then spent four months aboard the International Space Station as an Expedition 16 flight engineer in 2007–2008. His training took him from Russia’s Star City to an underwater habitat on NASA’s NEEMO-2 mission. He also served as a CAPCOM in Mission Control and led the Astronaut Office’s ISS branch. A third-generation Japanese American whose parents were interned at Topaz during World War II, he holds bachelor’s and master’s degrees in mechanical engineering from MIT. His career spans aerospace, education and nonprofit work. Today, he is Chief Development Officer at Iris.Aero in Virginia.

Daniel’s appearance at TEDxBelgrade is supported by the U.S. Embassy in Serbia as the United States marks 250 years of independence. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
